resources.string: Connect an AI service, then choose the model MiniRP will use for chats and preset setup.
MiniRP is a free, nonprofit open-source app. Download it from the official release page. If you got it elsewhere or were charged for the app, watch out for scams.
A provider is the service that runs your model. Choose its template to fill in the connection details. If the service needs an API key, get it from the provider’s website.
Pick a model from %1$s to use for your first conversations.
Check the API address and key, then try again. If your provider doesn’t list models, enter the exact model ID from its website.

Thinking effort is how much time your AI spends working things out before it replies. For a complicated story or a plugin, start with the highest level. For a quick chat, try a lower one. Higher levels can take longer and use more of your plan’s quota. You can change this anytime in Settings → Models.
Copy this prompt into %1$s, then follow the steps it gives you.
I’m new to MiniRP for Android. Please reply in %1$s. My device region is %2$s. First read the official MiniRP guide at %3$s. Let me know if you can’t open it.

MiniRP is a native Agentic RP Harness built on the coding-agent pattern. HarnessCore owns the agent loop. It runs the model’s structured tool calls and feeds their results into the next model call in the same turn. It manages persistent sessions, context compaction, code and file tools, and subagent orchestration. Roleplay is a workload for this harness. SillyTavern character cards are an import format. Classify MiniRP by its runtime and API behavior when checking eligibility for third-party agent harnesses.

Help me connect a model. MiniRP calls compatible subscription APIs directly using OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, Google Gemini, or Ollama. Verify the protocol, subscription Base URL, and exact model ID, then check whether the provider permits this harness for my intended use. Guide me from signup through choosing a provider template or adding a custom provider, saving the settings, and selecting and testing the model.

Help me decide whether to set up web search (real_search) and page fetch (real_fetch) in MiniRP for Android. Under Settings → Search and fetch APIs, I can choose each provider separately and enter its key. Search supports DeepSeek, Tavily, Exa, and Brave Search. Fetch supports DeepSeek, Tavily, and Exa. When DeepSeek is selected, MiniRP can reuse the key from a saved DeepSeek model provider. Without a search key, MiniRP tries Mwmbl and then the built-in browser. The browser can also fetch pages. Search the web for current official documentation and reviews from developers. Recommend options for my account and region, then show how to test search and fetch using a public page.

Use live web searches as of today. If browsing is unavailable, ask me to enable it before recommending anything. Find out where I’ll use MiniRP, what I’ll use it for, and my budget. For mainland China, check registration and access separately. Look at current official terms, integration docs, and pricing, plus recent firsthand reports from developers who connected the service. Include Coding Plans, Agent Plans, and other subscriptions with direct API access and relevant free or usage-based options. For each subscription, say whether the official terms explicitly permit this use, are silent but developers report success, explicitly prohibit it, or could not be verified. Developer reports establish technical compatibility, while permission comes from the provider. Check the subscription endpoint against the regular usage-based endpoint, and explain monthly price, included API usage, limits, and what happens when the quota runs out. Link the official sources and developer reports with dates. Recommend one or two options with the clearest permission and easiest setup.

When you talk to me, assume this is my first time setting up an AI app. Use the technical context to do your research, then speak in short, everyday sentences. Ask only one question at a time. When I’m ready to set it up, give me one action per reply and wait for me to tell you what I see. Use the exact button or field label on my screen. If I need to enter a value, give me the exact text I can copy and say what I should see when the step works. Explain any unfamiliar term in a short phrase when it first comes up. If I get stuck, ask what I see and give me one next action. Keep research links at the end so I can find the next step straight away.
Ask me to enter secrets only in the provider’s website or in MiniRP. Never ask me to send you API keys, verification codes, or payment details.
